title: Job 39
paragraphs: ¹ "Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the deer brings forth her fawn? ² Do you count the months till they give birth? Do you know the time when they drop their young? ³ They crouch, they deliver their young, they are rid of their labor pains. ⁴ Their young grow strong and thrive in the wild; they leave and do not return.

⁶ I made the wilderness his home, the barren salt flats his dwelling. ⁷ He laughs at the commotion of the city; he hears no shouts from the driver. ⁸ He roams the hills as his pasture and searches for any green thing. ⁹ Will the wild ox agree to serve you? Will it spend the night beside your manger? ¹⁰ Can you hold it to the furrow with a harness? Will it plow the valleys behind you?

¹¹ Will you rely on it for its great strength? Will you leave your heavy work to it? ¹² Can you trust it to haul in your grain and bring it to your threshing floor? ¹³ The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they like the feathers of the stork or falcon? ¹⁴ She lays her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand, ¹⁵ unmindful that a foot may crush them, or that some wild animal may trample them.

¹⁶ She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers; she does not care if her labor was in vain — ¹⁷ for God has made her forget wisdom; he has given her no share of understanding. ¹⁸ Yet when she rises and spreads her wings, she laughs at horse and rider. ¹⁹ Have you given the horse its strength? Have you clothed its neck with a flowing mane? ²⁰ Can you make it leap like a locust? Its proud snorting is terrifying!

²¹ It paws the ground in the valley, exulting in its strength; it charges into battle. ²² It laughs at fear and is not frightened; it does not shy away from the sword. ²³ The quiver rattles against its side, the flashing spear and javelin. ²⁴ With fierce energy it devours the ground; it cannot stand still when the battle trumpet sounds. ²⁵ At each blast of the horn it snorts, 'Aha!' It catches the scent of battle from afar, the thunder of commanders and the battle cry.

²⁶ Is it by your wisdom that the hawk takes flight and spreads its wings toward the south? ²⁷ Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest on high? ²⁸ It dwells on the rocky crag, on the steep face of rock and cliff. ²⁹ From there it hunts for food; its eyes scan the distant horizon. ³⁰ Its young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there it is."
